Wait, the M square is still at (24, 28)! I clicked it at (24, 28) which moved it to (23, 27), then ACTION7 moved it back to (24, 28). So the M square is back at (24, 28), not at (25, 29) as I expected.
The issue is that clicking the M square moves it up-left, and ACTION7 moves it down-right. So to move the M square down-right, I need to use ACTION7 without clicking it first.
But ACTION7 moves the "last-clicked" M square. So I need to click the M square to select it, then use ACTION7 to move it down-right. But clicking also moves it up-left!
So the sequence is:
1. Click M at (24, 28) → M moves to (23, 27)
2. ACTION7 → M moves to (24, 28) (back to original)
This means I can't move the M square down-right without first moving it up-left. Each "down-right" move requires a click (up-left) followed by ACTION7 (down-right), which results in no net movement.
Wait, that's not right. Let me reconsider.
When I click the M square, it moves up-left by 1. Then ACTION7 moves the last-clicked M square down-right by 1. So the sequence click+ACTION7 results in no net movement.
But if I click the M square and then DON'T use ACTION7, the M square moves up-left by 1.
And if I use ACTION7 without clicking first, it moves the last-clicked M square down-right by 1.
So to move the M square down-right, I need to:
1. Click the M square (to select it) → M moves up-left by 1
2. ACTION7 → M moves down-right by 1 (back to original)
3. ACTION7 again → M moves down-right by 1 (now at original + 1 down-right)
So to move the M square down-right by 1, I need to click it once and then use ACTION7 twice. The net effect is: up-left + down-right + down-right = down-right by 1.
Let me try this: click M at (24, 28), then ACTION7 twice.
Actually wait, let me re-examine. After clicking M at (24, 28), it moves to (23, 27). Then ACTION7 moves it to (24, 28). If I use ACTION7 again, it should move to (25, 29).
Let me try this.
